transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been having a really hard time focusing and sustaining my attention on tasks lately. I also find myself constantly losing things that I need, like my keys, wallet, or important papers. It's gotten to the point where it's really starting to disrupt my daily life.
Do you also find yourself feeling very restless, fidgety, interrupting others, or acting before thinking, or is it mainly problems with attention and losing things?

Honestly, it is a mix of both. Along with struggling to focus and constantly losing my things, I frequently interrupt people or butt into their conversations and activities. I also find it really hard to just relax and do leisure activities quietly.
Have these attention and restlessness symptoms been present since childhood, before age 12, and have they caused problems in more than one setting like home, school, or work?

Yes, I've definitely had these issues since I was a kid, well before age 12, but they've been a constant, major struggle for about a year and a half now. They definitely cause a lot of difficulties in my daily life, both at home and at work.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation). The new information supports this diagnosis rather than changing the differential: the patient has both inattentive symptoms (difficulty sustaining attention, losing things) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (interrupting, difficulty relaxing quietly), with onset before age 12 and impairment in more than one setting (home and work). No evidence was introduced for an alternative diagnosis, so the candidate list remains the same.
